body.input: Which AI companies opened an office in Denmark in 2026?

response.content:
Based on available information, I was unable to find a comprehensive list of AI companies that opened an office in Denmark specifically in 2026. However, here are some relevant developments I found:

- **FPT Software** — The Vietnamese IT company expanded its European presence by opening a new office in Denmark, with a focus on AI-powered solutions and digital transformation services.

- **Sapient Perception** — A Copenhagen-based deep-tech startup building AI-powered sensing infrastructure for unmanned systems (defense and security). Founded by former Phase One engineers, it is operating from Copenhagen.

Beyond individual office openings, Denmark has been actively strengthening its AI ecosystem in 2026:

- The **Danish Centre for AI Innovation (DCAI)**, which operates the Gefion AI supercomputer, received a DKK 500 million (~€67 million) investment in November 2026, with **Netcompany** joining as a new co-owner alongside the Novo Nordisk Foundation and EIFO. This signals growing AI infrastructure investment in the country.

- The Danish government's 2026 platform includes ambitions to make Denmark a frontrunner in responsible AI development.

If you are looking for a specific company or type of AI company, I'd be happy to refine the search.

context.content:
Together, the partners aim to strengthen a shared sovereign national AI platform that reduces barriers for advanced AI adoption, particularly for public institutions, regulated industries and smaller businesses. The partnership brings together DCAI’s advanced AI infrastructure with Netcompany’s experience in developing and operating some of Europe’s most complex and society-critical digital systems.

The investment also supports Denmark’s ambition, as set out in the 2026 government platform, to become a frontrunner in the development and responsible application of AI. The government intends to provide DKK 150 million to increase public commitment through EIFO. [...] “AI is fundamentally changing our economy and society, and within only five years, we expect the demand for AI capacity in Denmark to increase at least sixfold. Danish access to a strong and sovereign AI-infrastructure is therefore essential. By investing further in DCAI, we are building on what we have already created and quickly securing more AI capacity anchored in Denmark – and with perspectives that extend into Europe,” says Peder Lundquist, CEO, EIFO. [...] “When Gefion was inaugurated in 2024, the main task was to train large AI models. Today, companies and public organisations are building AI into their products and workflows, and a new generation of AI agents is taking on more complex tasks. DCAI will now be able to build modern AI capacity that public institutions and businesses can trust and adopt, not least where data is sensitive or regulated,” says Martin Svensson, CEO of DCAI.

Turning AI potential into progress for Denmark and EuropeBuilding on the foundation set by EIFO and the Novo Nordisk Foundation, DCAI’s ambition can now be further raised to give Danish innovation the power to grow, Danish research the capacity to lead and businesses of all sizes access to world-class AI capabilities on competitive terms.

document.name: Denmark’s AI supercomputer Gefion enters next chapter strengthening responsible and sovereign AI with new ownership and DKK 500 million investment - Novo Nordisk Fonden

context.content:
Denmark is pouring another 500 million DKK (approximately €67 million) into one of the world's most powerful supercomputers, backed by pharmaceutical giant Novo Nordisk Foundation, under plans announced on Tuesday.

The funding will support its supercomputer Gefion's infrastructure and operations at the Danish Centre for AI Innovation (DCAI), which runs the machine, according to an announcement from the Export and Investment Fund of Denmark.

Further details of how the funding will be used and when the additional capacity will be available have not been revealed.
